title: Middle-Elbe Experimental Medicine And Technology Intervention Platform
summary:
As people age, the brain's ability to stay mentally sharp and capable in everyday life can change – this is referred to as "cognitive vitality." Cognitive vitality is important for an independent, self-determined life, but it is shaped by many factors: physical illness, stress, and also the way nerve cells interact within the brain. This study aims to better understand which physical and neurological factors help some people maintain their mental performance over many years, while others experience decline – including in relation to early signs of diseases such as dementia.

To this end, participants undergo a comprehensive assessment every three years: they complete questionnaires, wear devices that track activity and sleep (wearables), perform memory and concentration tests (including via smartphone), undergo a brain MRI scan, and provide a blood sample. From this data, we aim to identify factors that protect or threaten mental fitness in old age, in order to develop new approaches for prevention and treatment in the long term.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Written consent
- MRI eligibility
- German-speaking
Exclusion criteria:
- Dementia
- Anti-dementia medication
- Stroke with residual symptoms
- Acute depressive episode
- Contraindications for performing MRI examinations in the research context: cardiac pacemaker or defibrillator systems, extensive tattoos, cochlear implants, insulin pumps, cerebral and ocular vascular clips, metal fragments, fear of enclosed spaces (claustrophobia), implants not suitable for MRI, permanent make-up, microblading
